rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
F = qvB sinθ
ε = −N dΦ/dt
F = BIL

rows.text: Force on moving charge F = q(v×B); on a wire F = BIL sinθ.  ·  Faraday: EMF ε = −dΦ/dt; Lenz's law gives the sign (induced current opposes the change in flux).

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: m = ZIt = (E/96500)·It — E is the EQUIVALENT mass (M/n for M^n+); identify n first, then substitute.  ·  Trick 2: Products at electrodes: molten NaCl → Na at cathode, Cl2 at anode; aqueous NaCl (brine) → H2 at cathode (water reduced) — overpotential decides water vs metal ions.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: L = NΦ/I  ·  Trick 3: Same charge through cells in series: masses ∝ equivalent masses (second law) — the series numerical is one ratio.  ·  Trick 4: Charge bookkeeping: Q = I×t (seconds!), moles of electrons = Q/96500 — the unit trap is minutes.
